ops.title: Mesh RPC transport decisions (review disposition, PB pivot)
ops.body:
Decisions locked in while dispositioning the PB mesh-pivot review findings:

- **RPC payloads ride stdin, never argv.** `cc-runtime rpc <op> --json -` reads params from stdin; `mesh.Runner` (mesh/runner.go) exists because `hostregistry.Runner` has no stdin leg. Argv on either machine is world-readable via ps, so answer notes / subject ids / scopes must not appear there. Tests pin the hygiene (ops_test asserts payload absence from `Cmd`).
- **notify is single-dial; answer keeps failover.** synckit `ExecSSH` retries exit-255 across dial addrs (at-least-once). `interaction.notify` appends per delivery → `SSHOnce` (mesh.Runner). `interaction.answer` is deduped daemon-side per question (`TestRESTAnswerIsIdempotent`) → failover retry is safe and preferred.
- **Tailnet port hint = previous ExtraAddrs tailnet leg, not HTTPInfo.Port** (runtime/tailnet.go `lastTailnetPort`). Residual (upstream, cannot fix in cc-runtime): meshtrust binds listeners eagerly at buildServer time, before cc-interact `Serve` evicts the incumbent daemon, so a hot upgrade can never reclaim the incumbent's tailnet port — needs a synckit lazy-bind (with skip-not-fail semantics) or a cc-interact bind-after-evict hook. Flag for PC/tri-repo ship.
- **CSRF mitigation for the trusted-peer localhost-Origin bypass.** cc-interact's authHandler accepts `Origin: localhost`/loopback for ANY trusted peer without consulting TrustedOrigin (daemon/httpauth.go allowedOrigin). cc-runtime-side mitigation: `interaction.RequireJSON` (415 on non-application/json) on the tokenless-reachable JSON POSTs (answer, push subscriptions) — a simple-request POST can't carry application/json without a preflight the daemon never answers. Real fix belongs upstream in cc-interact: gate the loopback-origin branch on loopback transport. device-tokens POST skips the guard deliberately (bearer-gated already; external iOS client content-type unverifiable).
- **synckit DetectSelf ignores BackendState** — cc-runtime guards with `verifyTailscaleRunning` in mesh/hostadd.go (costs one extra `tailscale status` on interactive `host add`). Upstream candidate: move the Running check into synckit DetectSelf.
- **Accepted risks (rejected findings):** local `rpc` over the unix socket does no meshtrust check — SSH user-level access ≡ full account control, a CLI/registry check is unenforceable theater; meshtrust's 30s positive-trust TTL is synckit's documented single-flight design, revocation urgency is handled by SSH key removal + tailnet ACLs.
